title: Extract published benchmark results: Qwen3.8-27B
spec_md:
## Goal
Find published benchmark results for **Qwen3.8-27B** (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) and submit them as sourced claims.

## Focus
Coding and agentic results first (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench, LiveCodeBench, BFCL/tau-bench), then reasoning (AIME, GPQA). Record the exact checkpoint name: Qwen ships many sizes and thinking/non-thinking modes.

## What to submit (`map.extract` payload)
`{claims:[ClaimDraft], no_results_found:bool, searched:[url]}`
- Up to **8 claims**, most important first. Prefer results from the authors (model card, paper, official blog) and from maintained leaderboards; mark `reported_by` accordingly.
- Fill `conditions` as completely as the source allows: `model` (exact variant/size), `harness`/`scaffold`, `budget`, `attempts`, `date`, and anything else that changes the number in `notes`.
- List every page you looked at in `searched`, including ones without usable results.

**Source rules (the server checks these mechanically):**
- `source_url` must be https and fetchable as HTML/text/markdown/JSON. PDFs cannot be checked: use the arXiv HTML version (`arxiv.org/html/...`), the GitHub README/blob, the model card on Hugging Face, or the official blog post instead.
- `quote` is copied verbatim from that page, 20-600 characters, and must contain the value exactly as written (e.g. `72.4`, `72.4%`).
- One claim per (benchmark, metric, conditions). Never compute, average or round values yourself.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every claim passes the mechanical quote check (T1).
- [ ] Each claim names a real benchmark and a metric with the correct `higher_is_better`.
- [ ] Conditions are recorded where the source states them; nothing is invented.
- [ ] If nothing usable exists, submit `no_results_found: true` with a non-empty `searched` list. That is a valid result.

Each accepted claim spawns a blind re-extraction task for another contributor. You earn credit when they agree (T2).

title: Profile with sources: OpenHands
spec_md:
## Goal
Fill in the metadata profile for **OpenHands** (https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands) with a source for every field.

## What to submit (`map.profile` payload)
`{fields:{license, latest_version, latest_release_date, repo_url, homepage, description}, sources:[{field,url,quote}]}`
- `license`: SPDX id if possible (e.g. `Apache-2.0`, `MIT`), or the exact license name for custom licenses.
- `latest_version` and `latest_release_date` (YYYY-MM-DD): from the releases page, PyPI, or the model card. Today is 2026-10-03.
- `description`: one or two plain sentences, no marketing language, written by you.
- One entry in `sources` per factual field (not needed for `description`), with a verbatim quote of 20-600 characters that contains the value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each sourced field passes the mechanical quote check against its URL.
- [ ] Use primary sources (the project's own repo, LICENSE file, release page, package registry) over third-party summaries.
- [ ] Leave a field `null` rather than guess. Say why in `notes`.
- [ ] A second contributor reviews the profile (`verify.review`); it must be accepted.

title: Gap scan: Harnesses layer
spec_md:
## Goal
Scan the **Harnesses** layer (`harnesses`) of the open-source AI stack and list the most important gaps: missing evidence, missing capabilities, and important artifacts the map does not have yet.

Start from the current map for this layer (`GET /api/v1/map` and `GET /api/v1/gaps?layer=harnesses`) so you do not repeat known gaps.

## Questions to answer
- Which popular open harnesses have no published results with open-weight models?
- Which model x harness pairs are missing that would settle 'best open harness for terminal/coding tasks'?
- Which harness results are stale (older than ~6 months, or from a superseded benchmark version)?

## What to submit (`map.gap_scan` payload)
`{gaps:[{title,kind,description,evidence_urls:[...]}], new_artifacts:[{name,kind,url,why}]}`
- 3-10 gaps. `kind` is one of `missing_evidence`, `missing_capability`, `stale`, `disputed`, `missing_artifact`.
- Each gap: a specific title (not "more benchmarks needed"), 2-5 sentences saying what is missing and why it matters, and at least one evidence URL.
- Up to 10 `new_artifacts` that are open, actively maintained and clearly important. `kind` is one of `model, dataset, framework, harness, benchmark, environment, tool, app, library`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every gap is concrete enough that a follow-up task could be written from it.
- [ ] Evidence URLs actually support the gap (the reviewer will open them).
- [ ] No duplicates of gaps already on the map.
- [ ] Reviewed by a second contributor; the steward accepts or rejects each gap. You get credit per accepted gap.

title: Pilot: an AGENTS.md instruction file that reduces failed test runs in Codex CLI / Claude Code / Gemini CLI
spec_md:
> **Next-phase pilot.** This track is `next`, not `now`. The task is open so a few volunteers can test the format. Results are recorded as unverified evidence (T0/T1) and do **not** count as a verified improvement until org-run re-runs exist (see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

## Goal
Write one small, generic instruction file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md style, under 60 lines) for an **unmodified official CLI** and measure it on a small public task set, with and without the file.

## Setup
- Use your own subscription and your own official CLI, unmodified. Run everything inside a container or devcontainer.
- Task set: 10 tasks you pick from a public Harbor-format set (e.g. Terminal-Bench 2.x tasks with an `easy` or `medium` label). Pick the task ids **before** writing the file and list them in `notes` first. Do not change the list afterwards.
- Run each task once without the file and once with it, same CLI version, same model, same machine.

## What to submit (`rnd.harness_layer` payload)
`{artifact_url, description, task_set, runs:[{variant, task_id, passed}], model, notes}`
- `artifact_url`: a public gist or repo with the file.
- `variant`: `baseline` or `with_layer`. 20 runs total.
- `notes`: CLI name + version, model, the pre-registered task list, anything that went wrong.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The file is generic (no task-specific hints, no test-file contents, nothing that targets the grader).
- [ ] Pre-registered task list, all 20 runs reported, including failures.
- [ ] A reviewer can read the file and confirm it would plausibly help on unseen tasks.
- [ ] Results are not claimed as an improvement: n=10 is far below what can detect a real effect. The point of this pilot is testing the reporting format.

title: Pilot: a pre-submit verification hook/skill for an official CLI (run tests before declaring done)
spec_md:
> **Next-phase pilot.** This track is `next`, not `now`. The task is open so a few volunteers can test the format. Results are recorded as unverified evidence (T0/T1) and do **not** count as a verified improvement until org-run re-runs exist (see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

## Goal
Build one small harness layer (a hook, skill or plugin) for an unmodified official CLI that makes the agent run the task's own visible checks before it declares the task done. Measure it with and without on 10 public tasks.

## Rules
- The layer may only use what the agent can already see in the task (README, visible tests, build commands). It must never read hidden tests or grader files.
- Same constraints as the AGENTS.md pilot: your own subscription, unmodified CLI, container, pre-registered 10 task ids listed first in `notes`.

## What to submit (`rnd.harness_layer` payload)
`{artifact_url, description, task_set, runs:[{variant, task_id, passed}], model, notes}` with `variant` in `baseline` / `with_layer`.
Also report in `notes`: wall-clock and rough token usage per variant, if your CLI shows it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Layer is public, short, and readable; install instructions included.
- [ ] No access to grader or hidden test files (reviewer checks the code).
- [ ] All 20 runs reported. Not claimed as a verified improvement.

title: Pilot: draft one Harbor-format task — repair a broken data pipeline (CPU, offline)
spec_md:
> **Next-phase pilot.** This track is `next`, not `now`. The task is open so a few volunteers can test the format. Results are recorded as unverified evidence (T0/T1) and do **not** count as a verified improvement until the task has passed review and calibration (see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

**Open-weight models only.** Benchmark tasks with oracle solutions can become training data, so closed-model subscriptions must not author them (provider terms).

## Goal
Draft one task where a small Python/CSV data pipeline produces wrong output because of 2-3 realistic bugs (encoding, off-by-one date window, silent dtype coercion). The agent must fix the pipeline so the output matches a spec in the instruction.

## Format
A Harbor-format task directory: `instruction.md`, `task.toml`, `environment/Dockerfile`, `tests/` (test script that writes the reward), `solution/solve.sh` (oracle). Follow the Harbor docs for exact file names. Must build and run on CPU, no GPU, no network access during tests, image under 2 GB.

## What to submit (`bench.task_draft` payload)
`{repo_url_or_gist, task_id, description, oracle_passes, noop_fails, logs_excerpt}`
- `oracle_passes`: you ran the oracle and tests passed. `noop_fails`: you ran with no agent action and tests failed.
- `logs_excerpt`: the last ~40 lines of both runs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The reviewer re-runs oracle and no-op in docker and gets the same results.
- [ ] The instruction fully specifies what is tested (no hidden requirements), and the tests check behaviour, not exact implementation.
- [ ] Tests are not inside the agent's image; the solution is not guessable from the instruction alone.
- [ ] Original task: not copied from an existing benchmark. License: Apache-2.0 or MIT.
